Alex.confusing: Confused reports were hard to weigh: Blair's "confused" Kookaburra report and Drew's shifting roles made it unclear whose claims to trust. It also wasn't obvious that a Kookaburra visit confuses the visited player rather than the visitor.
Alex.fun: Round 2, when Finley's Eagle exposed Drew's "nobody visited me" story and the whole table converged on the contradiction.

Alex.regret: In round 1 I threw at Blair, who was actually Farm, based on an unexplained egg loss; I should have checked Drew and Casey's contradicting Owl and Falcon stories first.

Blair.confusing: The confused rule was hard to use: my dawn reports were unreliable, so my own Kookaburra reads (Casey as Floofer, Ellis as Owl) were wrong and I couldn't tell which claims to trust.

review.title: Three Farm Funerals
review.headline: Three rounds, three innocent Farm players eggsecuted, and nobody tested the pile-on.
review.summary: Every round ended with a Farm player eggsecuted. The table piled onto one outlier within a few beats and never tested the story. Round 1 hit a confused Kookaburra. Round 2 hit an honest Kookaburra whose report was blanked by a hug. Round 3 hit the true Turkey, who was contradicted by a Meowfia Sphinx. Ellis won at 11 by being Meowfia in round 2 and staying quiet in round 3.

rounds.recap: Blair was confused and lost 2 eggs, and his Floofer read on Casey was wrong. The table agreed he was the only odd story and threw at him. Drew was the lone Meowfia (Sphinx), falsely claimed Hawk, and won by joining the pile-on.

Blair (Meowfia Floofer) hugged Drew, so Drew's Kookaburra got no visitor effect. Finley's Eagle and Blair both said Blair visited Drew, and Drew's claim looked contradictory. Drew was thrown at by nearly everyone and was Farm. Blair and Ellis, the Meowfia, won.

Casey (Meowfia Sphinx) claimed Turkey, which Drew actually held. Drew was accused of copying the claim, even though Drew spoke before no one else had claimed it. Drew was eggsecuted as Farm and Casey won.

highlights.text: Blair the Floofer hugged Drew, and then used the hug's side effect, a missing visitor, to push Drew's claim as a lie.
Casey, Meowfia Sphinx, knew Alex was the Eagle and claimed the real Turkey role, framing Drew with a direct conflict.
Drew, the only Meowfia, simply agreed with the table and won with a low-risk 2-point throw.
Drew's last-ditch throw at Casey was correct, but nobody listened, and a Wild came back as the consolation.

confusions.what: Said no visitor and no confusion proved Blair lied, not realizing the Floofer's hug stops the Kookaburra's confusion effect.
Said Drew's 'not confused' report was the lie, though Drew had no reason to be confused if hugged.
Said Casey claimed Turkey 'earlier' and that Drew's earlier claims showed switching, when roles are re-dealt each round; the table blamed Drew for past-round roles.
Treated Drew's past-round claims (Hawk, Kookaburra) as evidence of lying, though roles are re-dealt every round.
Said Drew copied Casey's claim after Casey spoke, though Drew's claim was equally likely first in any order; also treated past-round claims as a tell.
Seemingly believed Casey's 'nobody visited me' while knowing Ellis visited Casey; fine as a lie cover, but Ellis did not point out Casey's claim was false and the table never noticed.

worked: Hug (Floofer): blanking a Kookaburra's confusion and creating a fake contradiction was a clever, subtle Meowfia play in round 2.
Sphinx: knowing a Farm role let Casey make a precise, plausible claim and a Turkey conflict in round 3.
Eagle/Falcon cross-checks: Alex and Finley's corroborating reports in round 3 gave real, verifiable evidence.
Consolation rule: Drew's returned card for throwing at the right team gave a reason to throw honestly.
problems: Farm lost every round: the pile-on dynamic makes the day a rush to a consensus target by beat 3, with CAW CAW ending it before real questions. Consider requiring 4 CAWs or a minimum beat count.

Confused Kookaburra is too punishing: the confused loss of 2 eggs made an innocent player the unexplained anomaly in round 1 and round 3. Consider making confusion less visible, or not letting it cost eggs.
Nobody asked cheap tests like 'who claims Turkey' early or used the nest-size list; players reasoned about past-round claims despite re-dealing, so a reminder that roles reset each round would help.

The Meowfia don't coordinate, but the one Meowfia player (Drew, Casey) just agreed with the table and won; with 1 Meowfia, lying has little cost. Score incentives for being the hidden Meowfia are strong.

Scores diverge oddly: the winner (Ellis) scored mostly from round 2, and Blair finished with 2 points after two Farm rounds ended with thrown cards lost. Throwing high cards at the consensus target is almost never costly, so throw size gave little signal.
